approach: Root cause: scope_guard.rs stores a pause as a file that line_pause trusts forever, and attempt_of marks an attempt as an environment stop only by the closing-reason prefix. Agent "did not complete" reasons for an expired login (401) or a usage limit carry no prefix, so that spend counts as line spend. Fix in six parts. (1) disk.rs gets AUTH_STOP and USAGE_LIMIT. `is_environment_reason` stays the one guard classifier: low disk, check timeout, auth stop and usage limit, each also accepted after the planning-stopped prefix. (2) New `disk::agent_stop_reason(who, detail)` builds the closing reason. It matches only the CLI's fixed API-error phrases, anchored at the start of the result text, and never for `error_max_*` subtypes. (3) It is called at every agent site that closes a job as Failed: the producer (producer.rs), the planner and the critic (planning.rs, which stop_planning prefixes, so the prefix is kept for the code that reads it). The verifier closes the job Rejected with a built candidate, a different path; it is a named, proposed follow-up, not an open question. (4) attempt_of calls `is_environment_reason`; T3 pauses on spend excluding every environment stop; the T3_LINE_DOLLARS flag still sees total spend. (5) Resuming stays narrow: a new `disk::resumable_reason` (low disk and check timeout only) serves `resumable_stop` and `settle_resume_marks`, so auth and usage stops leave no resume mark and a retry re-plans. (6) line_pause (callers: `go` at run/mod.rs and `retry` at reading.rs) recomputes signals from per-attempt records through a helper shared with try_watch_line, returns the stored pause only while the recompute still pauses, and otherwise deletes the file and returns None. Deleting the file still lifts a pause. Add tests, a CHANGELOG entry and a doc update.

decisions.choice: One classifier, `disk::is_environment_reason`, maps closing reasons to Verdict::Environment: LOW_DISK, CHECK_TIMEOUT, AUTH_STOP, USAGE_LIMIT, each also when it follows PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX (strip the prefix and leading space first). attempt_of calls it in place of its own starts_with(ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX).
decisions.reason: Criterion 2 asks for one function used by attempt_of. disk.rs owns the constants and the existing classifier, so the written reason and the guard share one definition. Accepting the planning prefix lets planner and critic stops classify while stop_planning keeps its prefix, which introspect.rs and reading.rs parse.

rejected.option: Keep attempt_of's starts_with(ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX) and add prefixes at call sites
rejected.why: Two places must agree, which is the drift that caused the class.

rejected.option: Match 401 or usage text inside attempt_of on any closing reason
rejected.why: Closing reasons carry free text from the work. Classification belongs where the reason is written, from the agent's failure detail.

rejected.option: Drop the planning prefix when the cause is environmental
rejected.why: introspect.rs (line 1289) and reading.rs (lines 1687, 4033) detect planning stops by that prefix; removing it would change introspection and retry seeding.

decisions.choice: `agent_stop_reason(who, detail)` classifies narrowly. The detail is `<subtype>: <text>` (claude.rs builds it). A subtype starting `error_max_` is never environment. Otherwise the trimmed text must START (case-insensitive) with a fixed CLI phrase: auth `API Error: 401`, `Invalid API key`, `Please run /login`, or text starting `API Error` that contains `authentication_error`; usage `Claude AI usage limit reached`, `You've hit your limit`. A match returns `environment: login expired: the <who> could not authenticate (<detail>); ...` or the usage form; anything else returns `the <who> did not complete: <detail>`.
decisions.reason: For a CLI API error the result text is the CLI's own message, which starts with the fixed phrase. A model's prose about 401 handling does not, and a producer that ran out of turns on auth code stays counted as work. A miss only means the old behaviour.

rejected.option: Substring match on '401', 'unauthorized', 'authentication' anywhere in the detail
rejected.why: A producer working on HTTP or auth code that ends with error_max_turns would drop out of T3, T1 and T4, which is the runaway case the guard exists to catch.

rejected.option: A typed cause on AgentOutput set in athena-agent
rejected.why: Cleaner, but it adds a field to every AgentOutput constructor and edits a crate outside the deliverables. Recorded as a follow-up.

decisions.choice: Route every agent site that closes a job Failed through agent_stop_reason: producer.rs line 206, planning.rs line 186 (planner) and line 332 (critic). stop_planning keeps prefixing; the classifier accepts the cause after the prefix. Leave run/mod.rs line 680 (keep_timed_out_work, a deadline with state TimedOut) unchanged.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The planner is the first agent a job runs, so a job dispatched after the login expired fails at the planner, and each retry would add a T1 attempt. Both planning sites build the reason from the same record.detail as the producer, so the same function serves them. Line 680 is a deadline: attempt_of maps TimedOut to Failed whatever the reason says, so an `environment:` reason there would make record and guard disagree. planning.rs is not in the brief's deliverable list but is not governance and falls under `crates/`.

rejected.option: Fix only the producer call site
rejected.why: One instance of the class; the planner and critic 401 still count as line spend.

rejected.option: Also change the timed-out path to close Failed when an auth cause is detected
rejected.why: It changes retry and kept-work behaviour of timed-out jobs and widens the change.

decisions.choice: The verifier's auth stop (run/verification.rs lines 219-224 into verify.rs line 307) is left out and recorded as a named, proposed follow-up in the CHANGELOG entry and docs/design/scope-guard.md: close a verifier auth or usage stop as Failed with an environment reason and a resume mark on the built candidate, the way a low-disk stop after the build already does, so `athena retry` resumes from the candidate and verifies again.
decisions.reason: Read: a verifier failure goes into the judgment reasons and the job closes Rejected with a verification record (verification.rs lines 358-362), not Failed. Reclassifying it in the guard alone would hide a rebuilt candidate's producer spend from T3 on each retry, because a retry would re-run the producer. The right fix is a new close-and-resume path, which is a separate behaviour change touching verify.rs, a file the brief marks dropped for the replay work.

rejected.option: Classify Rejected jobs whose reasons hold a verifier auth failure as Environment in attempt_of
rejected.why: It would exclude the producer's spend of a candidate that a retry rebuilds, so a loop of rebuild-then-401 would escape T3 and show only as the dollar flag; and it would read free-text reasons back.

rejected.option: Edit verify.rs line 307 to call agent_stop_reason
rejected.why: It would double the `did not complete` wording and leave the job Rejected, so the guard still counts it.

decisions.choice: Resuming stays narrow. Add `pub fn resumable_reason(reason)` in disk.rs, true only for LOW_DISK and CHECK_TIMEOUT with no planning-prefix stripping. `resumable_stop` and `settle_resume_marks` (run/mod.rs line 586) call it; `is_environment_reason` is the wider guard classifier used by attempt_of only.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. resumable_stop and resumed_candidate decide whether a retry resumes a kept candidate and whether T3 uses the verifier-share forecast. settle_resume_marks decides whether a closed job keeps its resume mark. An auth or usage stop at planning or producer has no candidate, so keeping the mark would let `athena retry` resume from nothing. Behaviour of both stays exactly as today.

rejected.option: Let resumable_stop and settle_resume_marks use the widened classifier
rejected.why: A retry after a 401 could be read as a resume of a candidate that does not exist and cut the forecast to the verifier share, pausing too early.

decisions.choice: t3_basis drops the spend of every Environment attempt and the `kept` logic goes; `resumed_last` still selects the verifier-share forecast. The T3_LINE_DOLLARS flag uses the line's TOTAL spend. facts() states the environment spend when there is some, computed from the attempts.
decisions.reason: Environment spend must not count toward progress-less spend; with the `kept` rule a [401 stop, low-disk stop] line still pauses. The flag never blocks dispatch, so a loop of environment stops stays visible without pausing the line.

rejected.option: Drop environment spend everywhere, including the dollar flag
rejected.why: A line that keeps hitting environment stops would show nothing.

rejected.option: Keep the `kept` rule and count redone environment spend toward the pause
rejected.why: This is what paused the failing jobs; resumed_retry_is_judged_on_remaining_stages encodes it and is updated.

rejected.option: Add an environment-spend field to MarkNumbers
rejected.why: It changes the stored mark format for no signal; facts() can compute it.

decisions.choice: The pause stays a file, only as the lift handle and display text. line_pause returns it only while a fresh evaluation (shared helper `line_signals`) is at Level::Pause; otherwise it removes the file and returns None. try_watch_line removes a pause file when the level is below Pause. The helper takes p90 from the latest request in the line with a positive forecast, falling back to 0.
decisions.reason: The pause is derived from per-attempt stop reasons under the current rule on every check, so a rule change or reclassified stop clears a stale pause. line_pause runs at dispatch of a retry whose request may have no reading yet, so it must not read p90 as 0 and clear a real T3 pause. Both callers, `go` (run/mod.rs line 696) and `retry` (reading.rs line 1036), get the same behaviour.

rejected.option: Compute the pause purely from records, with no file
rejected.why: The documented lift (delete the file) would stop working and a deleted file would be recreated by a read.

rejected.option: Store a rule version in the mark and compare it
rejected.why: More state and a migration for existing files; recomputing under the current rules needs neither.

rejected.option: A one-off cleanup of existing pause files
rejected.why: It works around instances; the recompute clears them on the next check.

decisions.choice: No CHANGELOG-reading test. Criterion 1 is checked by Grep on CHANGELOG.md.
decisions.reason: Criterion 1 is a content criterion; a test pinned to Unreleased wording breaks at the next release and shows no behaviour.

rejected.option: include_str! test of the Unreleased section
rejected.why: It breaks when the entry moves under a version heading or is reworded.

decisions.choice: docs/design/scope-guard.md states that `athena status` lists the stored pause file as is, that a pause holds only while a signal fires (checked at the next dispatch or retry of that line), and names the verifier follow-up.
decisions.reason: status does not reconcile, so it can show a pause the next check clears; documenting this avoids widening code.

rejected.why: Extra CLI code outside the deliverables.

decisions.choice: Criterion 6 is shown by running the repository's own gate commands over the workspace. ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX stays a `pub const` referenced by tests and the new constants' tests, so no dead-code warning arises when attempt_of stops using it.
decisions.reason: The gate is the production check Athena runs; the source tree is the seam, with no double.

rejected.why: disk.rs and scope_guard.rs tests reference it and it documents the prefix the reasons share.

Add `agent_stop_reason(who, detail)` with the anchored matcher and the error_max_ exclusion. Add `resumable_reason` (low disk and check timeout only) and make `resumable_stop` use it. Unit tests for all of it.

Shared `line_signals` helper with p90 selection. line_pause recomputes and clears a stale pause. try_watch_line removes a pause file when the level is below Pause. Update the Verdict::Environment and ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX docs. New tests; update the two existing tests; a Plan producer_errors field and rig wrapper.

New test `a_planner_or_critic_auth_stop_is_an_environment_stop`: a scripted 401 on the planner and on the critic closes the job Failed with an environment reason, request_records reads Verdict::Environment, and no resume mark is left.

steps: Read the scope_guard.rs `watcher_tests` module (Plan, Rig, rig_with_space, write_mark, mark, the T3 tests `resumed_retry_is_judged_on_remaining_stages` and `retry_refuses_paused_line`) and the `facts` function; check how the fake charges cost on an Error turn and how retry_refuses_paused_line reaches the refusal (go or retry). disk.rs: add `pub const AUTH_STOP: &str = "environment: login expired"` and `pub const USAGE_LIMIT: &str = "environment: usage limit reached"`. Add a private `environment_cause(detail: &str) -> Option<&'static str>`: split the detail at the first `: ` into subtype and text, return None when the subtype starts with `error_max_`, otherwise compare the trimmed text's case-insensitive START against the fixed phrases (auth: `API Error: 401`, `Invalid API key`, `Please run /login`, or starts with `API Error` and contains `authentication_error`; usage: `Claude AI usage limit reached`, `You've hit your limit`). Add `pub fn agent_stop_reason(who: &str, detail: &str) -> String`: on a match return `{AUTH_STOP}: the {who} could not authenticate ({detail}); this is the environment, not the work. Log in again, then retry the job` (or the usage form); otherwise `the {who} did not complete: {detail}`.

disk.rs: make `is_environment_reason` strip an optional `athena_data::records::PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX` plus leading space, then accept LOW_DISK, CHECK_TIMEOUT, AUTH_STOP, USAGE_LIMIT. Add `pub fn resumable_reason(reason: &str) -> bool` (LOW_DISK or CHECK_TIMEOUT only, no stripping) and make `resumable_stop` use it. Update doc comments. scope_guard.rs production code: `attempt_of` computes `environment` with `crate::disk::is_environment_reason`. In `t3_cost` the pause test uses that spend and the `T3_LINE_DOLLARS` flag uses the total cost of all attempts. In `facts()` add the environment spend to the T3 detail when above 0. Update the doc comments of `t3_basis` and `t3_cost`.

scope_guard.rs: add a private helper `line_signals(records, requests, line) -> (Vec<AttemptRecord>, Signals, f64)` that calls line_attempts, takes p90 from the latest request in the line with a positive forecast_p90_dollars (else 0), and calls evaluate_before_attempt. try_watch_line uses it and removes the pause file whenever its level is below Pause (the flag file when None). `line_pause` reads the stored pause, recomputes with the helper and returns the mark only when `overall() == Level::Pause`; otherwise it removes the file and returns None. line_pause never creates a pause file. Document that `go` (run/mod.rs) and `retry` (reading.rs) both call it.

Add unit tests for [Environment, Environment] at Level::None everywhere, [Failed small, Environment big] not pausing, and environment-only spend above T3_LINE_DOLLARS giving a Flag and no Pause. Add `a_stale_pause_is_cleared_when_nothing_fires` (both stale cases, through go and retry) and `a_real_pause_survives_the_recompute` (same-criterion pause, T3 pause with a reading-less retry, deleting the file lifts).

risks.mitigation: Fixed CLI phrases anchored at the start of the result text, with error_max_ subtypes excluded. Tests show work text that mentions 401 and authentication stays a plain reason. A miss leaves the old behaviour; a wrong match drops one attempt from the pause counts, and its dollars still reach the line-dollar flag.

risks.risk: line_pause clears a pause that should hold, for example when the retry request's reading has no forecast p90.
risks.mitigation: One shared helper, `line_signals`, serves the watcher and line_pause. p90 comes from the latest request in the line with a positive forecast. Tests: a real same-criterion pause and a real T3 pause with a reading-less retry both survive the recompute, through both `go` and `retry`.

risks.risk: line_pause now deletes a file, and it has a second caller (`retry` in reading.rs) beyond `go`.
risks.mitigation: Both callers named in the plan and docs; the stale and real tests drive `retry` as well as `go`. The deletion only happens when the recompute no longer pauses, and never creates a file.

risks.risk: Dropping all environment spend in t3_basis changes the behaviour tested by resumed_retry_is_judged_on_remaining_stages.
risks.mitigation: Update the test as decided and keep a control showing a plain failure with the same spend still pauses. The change is stated in the CHANGELOG and docs.

risks.risk: A line stuck in repeated environment stops now has no pause bound.

risks.risk: A verifier 401 still counts as a rejection, so the class stays partly open.
risks.mitigation: Named as a proposed follow-up with its design (Failed plus environment reason plus resume mark on the built candidate) in the CHANGELOG and scope-guard doc; the reason it is not done here is the new close-and-resume path it needs.

risks.risk: retry_refuses_paused_line and other tests plant a hand-written pause that the recompute now clears.
risks.mitigation: Step 8 rewrites them. The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard` and the whole suite.

demonstrations.method: New watcher tests `a_stale_pause_is_cleared_when_nothing_fires` and `a_real_pause_survives_the_recompute` call `Athena::line_pause(&records, job_id)`, `Athena::go` and `Athena::retry` (the reading.rs caller at line 1036), so both callers of line_pause are covered. Stale: (a) a line with one environment-stopped attempt and a pause file planted with `write_mark(r.pause(&a), &mark("pause", a, "T3"))`; (b) two rejections for different criteria (`rig(0.8, 0.01, &[Some(0), Some(1)])`, so no T4) with a planted T4 pause. For each, line_pause is None, the file is gone, `go` on the line is dispatched, and in a second pass over a freshly planted stale file `retry` is not refused. Real: two rejections for the same criterion (`&[Some(0), Some(0)]`, pause written by the watcher) and a T3 line (`rig(1.0, 0.8, &[Some(0)])`) whose retry has no reading yet, which exercises the p90 fallback; line_pause returns the mark, the file exists, `go` and `retry` refuse with the signal text, and deleting the file lifts the pause. The existing `retry_refuses_paused_line` is rewritten to use the watcher's own pause.
demonstrations.observes: Stale cases: line_pause is None, the pause file no longer exists, `go` dispatches and `retry` is not refused. Real cases: the stored mark is returned, the file still exists, both entry points refuse with the signal text; deleting the file lifts a real pause as before.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base commit line_pause reads the file and returns the stored mark, so the assertions that line_pause is None, that the file is gone, and that `go` and `retry` proceed all fail. The real-pause assertions pass on both base and change, which shows the recompute does not clear real pauses.
